subject: Post-call: Quantaflow POC sizing, latency SLOs, and deployment topology
messages:
From: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>
To: Claire Young <claire.young@quantaflow.com>, Daniel Park <daniel.park@quantaflow.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 20 Nov 2026 10:23:00 -0800
Subject: Post-call recap & recommended POC sizing (Quantaflow)

Claire / Daniel — thanks again for the call this morning. Quick recap and recommended next steps so we have a single source of truth for the POC sizing and SLAs we discussed. Attachment: redwood-slo-options.xlsx and service-topology-diagram.png (see short stubs attached).

Key pain points you emphasized:
- Real-time enrichment on user queries: 200–400 QPS at peak across API gateway.
- Hard 95/99 latency targets for classification+context: 95th <= 180ms, 99th <= 420ms (tail matters).
- PHI in payloads for a subset of customers — on-prem or VPC-only processing required.
- Cost sensitivity for sustained throughput; ability to fall back to cheaper model variant on surge.

Goal for the POC:
- Demonstrate production-grade 95/99 latency at representative load with real prompt set, and demonstrate private VPC deployment for PHI customers.
- Validate KV/prefix caching reduces compute by ~30% for common prefixes.
- Produce estimate for cost/QPS across hosted vs dedicated vs private deployment options.

Technical recommendations (summary):
1) Model surface
   - Primary: Llama3-13B-v1 quantized to int8 for steady-state; 13B chosen for lower tail latency and cheaper unit cost.
   - Secondary (fallback): Llama3-70B-qat (or 70B-8bit) for higher-quality responses when latency budget allows.
2) Sizing proposal for POC (examples)
   - Private VPC (PHI subset): 2 x H100 (dedicated pool) configured with continuous batching disabled for latency-sensitive routes; KV-cache on prefix store. Start with 2 nodes, target ~250 QPS with 95th projection ~170ms.
   - Hosted/dedicated for general traffic: 4 x A100xlarge equivalent (or 8 x A100-passthrough cores depending on packing) with batching window 5–10ms for cost efficiency.
3) Caching & batching
   - KV prefix cache enabled (expect 25–40% token compute reduction for common flows).
   - Conservative batching configuration for low-latency calls: max_batch_delay 10ms, max_tokens_per_batch tuned to keep 95th under 180ms.
4) Routing & fallbacks
   - Smart routing: route PHI requests to Private VPC cluster; non-PHI to Hosted/Dedicated. On capacity pressure, automatically fall back to 13B quantized model for latency-sensitive endpoints, or to a rate-limited queue for non-critical workflows.
5) Observability & acceptance criteria
   - 7-day pilot with synthetic and replayed real traffic. Acceptance: 95th <= 180ms and 99th <= 420ms on 90% of test windows, clear cost/QPS delta documented.

Immediate asks / next steps
- Claire: share sample prompt set and a small redacted PHI sample for local benchmarking (S3 link ok).
- Quantaflow security: provide SOC2 contact and any required questionnaire (we flagged SOC2 items on the call).
- Marissa / Karthik: produce preliminary cost and node-count estimate and a bench plan (see internal note below).

I'll schedule a short engineering sync next week to agree on the exact replay plan. Thanks — Marcus

--
Marcus Lin
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
marcus.lin@redwood.com | +1 (415) 555-0192
[Attachment: redwood-slo-options.xlsx (XLSX), service-topology-diagram.png (PNG)]

From: Claire Young <claire.young@quantaflow.com>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>
Cc: Daniel Park <daniel.park@quantaflow.com>
Date: Fri, 20 Nov 2026 13:02:00 -0500
Subject: Re: Post-call recap & recommended POC sizing (Quantaflow)

Thanks Marcus — this is great and captures the call well. A couple clarifications from our side:
- The 200–400 QPS is aggregate across regions; initial POC will focus on us-west traffic (~65% of total).
- PHI flows are roughly 12% of requests and must stay in our VPC; rest can go to Redwood-hosted or Dedicated.
- Procurement: we can sign an MSA + PO within 30 days if POC proves the SLOs.

Action items from Quantaflow:
- I'll upload a 1k sample of redacted prompts and a small PHI sample (S3 link) by Mon 11/23.
- Our security team will send the SOC2 questionnaire in a separate email (Daniel cc'd) — expect that early next week.

We prefer the private VPC topology for the PHI customers and demo the hosted/dedicated mix for non-PHI. Looking forward to the bench results.

Claire
Claire Young
Head of Platform Engineering, Quantaflow
claire.young@quantaflow.com | +1 (212) 555-0128

From: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
Cc: Claire Young <claire.young@quantaflow.com>, Daniel Park <daniel.park@quantaflow.com>
Date: Mon, 22 Nov 2026 09:30:00 -0800
Subject: Internal: POC bench plan + ask list (Quantaflow)

Marissa / Karthik — looping you in with the concrete asks from Quantaflow and the high-level sizing I sketched. Please see attachments and my recommended bench plan below (also attached: redwood-slo-options.xlsx).

Bench plan (short)
- Dataset: use Claire's 1k prompts + 200 PHI prompts once available.
- Workloads: steady sustained QPS at 50, 200, 350 QPS with 5-minute ramp windows; burst tests to 600 QPS to evaluate fallback behavior.
- Metrics: p50/p95/p99 token latency, end-to-end request latency, tokens/sec, GPU utilization, KV cache hit rate.

Proposed quick node configs to test (order matters):
A) Private VPC (latency-first): 2 x H100 (16GB) dedicated nodes with KV cache; no batching, or batching window <= 5ms.
B) Dedicated-hosted mix (cost/efficiency): 4 x A100-equivalent nodes with small batching (10ms).
C) Fallback variant: quantized Llama3-70B running on 2 x H100 for quality/latency tradeoff checks.

Immediate internal asks
- Marissa: cost/QPS delta for A vs B above and per-hour pilot estimate for 7 days.
- Karthik: run a quick local int8 quant profile on the 13B baseline and report expected memory/throughput delta. Also surface any model kernel concerns for 70B-8bit.
- Presales: prep a short one-slide ops runbook showing routing, fallbacks, and how we'd isolate PHI in the VPC.

I’ll tentatively schedule two 60-minute bench sessions: Wed 11/24 (initial) and Fri 11/26 (stress + fallback). Claire — if those conflict with your team’s holiday schedules, tell me and I’ll move.

Thanks — Marcus

--
Marcus Lin
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
marcus.lin@redwood.com
[Attachment: redwood-slo-options.xlsx]

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Cc: Claire Young <claire.young@quantaflow.com>
Date: Mon, 22 Nov 2026 18:05:00 +0530
Subject: Re: Internal: POC bench plan + ask list (Quantaflow)

Quick notes from a technical perspective — keeping these short so we can act: 

1) Int8 profile (13B)- Ran a quick quant profile on a dev replica: int8 reduces model memory by ~45% and improves throughput ~1.8x vs fp16 for small batch sizes. Tail latency improvement is modest (~10–15%) but cost wins are material. We should include an int8 fallback profile in the POC.

2) KV cache expectations- If Quantaflow's traffic has common prefixes (they indicated many templates), a 30–35% token compute reduction is realistic. We should capture a prefix-hit histogram from their sample prompts ASAP to tune cache size.

3) Networking & VPC notes- For PHI flows in the customer's VPC we'll need a secure peering/VPN with static egress IPs for audit evidence. Also recommend pre-warming containers for the PHI cluster to avoid cold-start tail spikes on first traffic day.

4) Bench requirements- Need: (a) sample prompts, (b) expected average tokens per request, (c) a representative token distribution (p50/p95 tokens). Claire — if you can include average tokens and percent of long-form requests in the sample upload, that will help our projections.

I'll prepare a short benchmarking playbook and a one-page cost/QPS table for Marissa to slot numbers into.

- Karthik
Karthik Iyer
Staff Infra Engineer | Redwood Inference
